author_or_org: James C. Davis, Paschal C. Amusuo, Tanmay Singla, Berk Çakar, Kirsten A. Davis

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Generative AI shifts software engineering from scarce implementation effort toward abundant, low-cost code production.
claims.quote: Generative AI is shifting software engineering from a practice organized around scarce implementation effort toward one organized around abundant, low-cost code production.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The source's evidence is a first-person case study, not a controlled productivity experiment.
claims.quote: We study this problem through a first-person case study: a 12-week development effort in which a single expert software engineer used frontier AI coding agents to build a document accessibility remediation system.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: A single expert software engineer used frontier AI coding agents over a 12-week effort to build a document accessibility remediation system.
claims.quote: We study this problem through a first-person case study: a 12-week development effort in which a single expert software engineer used frontier AI coding agents to build a document accessibility remediation system.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The empirical record comprises 88 contemporaneous field notes, 420 KLOC of production code, and 1.16 MLOC of tests, lints, documentation, and agent tooling.
claims.quote: The empirical record comprises 88 contemporaneous field notes, 420 KLOC of production code, and 1.16 MLOC of tests, lints, supporting documentation, and agent tooling.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The paper develops a candidate middle-range theory of governance conversion, expressed as a process model explaining how high-velocity agentic implementation becomes governable.
claims.quote: From this record, we develop a candidate middle-range theory of governance conversion, expressed as a process model explaining how high-velocity agentic implementation becomes governable.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The model explains that agentic implementation velocity surfaces recurring structural failure classes, and engineering judgment sustains velocity by converting those failures into durable governance mechanisms.
claims.quote: The model explains how agentic implementation velocity surfaces recurring structural failure classes, and how engineering judgment sustains velocity by converting those failures into durable governance mechanisms.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Existing governance models derive controls from known obligations, while governance conversion explains controls discovered from failures visible only during agentic work.
claims.quote: In contrast to existing governance models that derive controls from known obligations, governance conversion explains how controls are discovered from failures that become visible only during agentic work.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The central engineering problem is organizing architectures, tools, evidence, and feedback loops so AI-mediated development remains inspectable, correctable, and maintainable.
claims.quote: This shift changes the central engineering problem: not whether AI can generate useful code, but how engineers organize architectures, tools, evidence, and feedback loops so that AI-mediated development remains inspectable, correctable, and maintainable.
